title: The Burnt Extraction
premise: Gideon Joubert, a burnt-out interpreter for a fragile peace delegation, is the only person who remembers a charter flight that officially never existed — because the delegation was aboard it when it was diverted mid-air and everyone's memories were chemically blurred. When Gideon's insomnia cracks the false memories loose, they discover a second attack is scheduled to destroy the peace talks and be written off as an accident. Racing a countdown they can barely prove is real, Gideon must decide whether to trust a handler who may have authored the erasure, expose the truth and shatter the delegation, or let the lie stand to save lives. In the end Gideon broadcasts the flight's real passenger manifest mid-attack, sacrificing their career and their last safe identity — and walks away as the sole keeper of what actually happened.
about_author: Cyrus Vasquez spent a decade working as a contract translator in conflict zones before turning to fiction, drawing on the strange intimacy of speaking other people's words for a living. He writes from a coastal town he declines to name, and claims he still can't remember his dreams.

chapters.title: The Hour That Won't Close
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Gideon wakes at 3:17 a.m. again, unable to sleep since the delegation's charter flight, haunted by a smell of burnt wiring that shouldn't be there. At the talks, a colleague mentions the flight was 'uneventful,' and the wrongness of that word itches. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Manifest of Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Digging through delegation records, Gideon finds the flight number missing from every database, boarding passes blank, photos of the cabin smudged. Only their own handwritten notes survive. A security officer, Ilsa Renner, watches them too closely. Emotional beat: gaslit paranoia sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Interpreter Heard
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. During a tense translation session, a phrase in the foreign delegation's side room triggers a flash: screaming, oxygen masks, a pilot's voice saying 'not an accident.' Gideon misrenders a sentence deliberately to buy time, first small betrayal of the process. Emotional beat: guilt and adrenaline entwined.

chapters.title: Renner's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa Renner. Renner, the delegation's security chief, reviews Gideon's file and a sealed directive: observe, do not intervene. She suspects Gideon's memories are returning ahead of schedule. She burns one document but keeps a copy — loyalty already splitting down the middle. Emotional beat: cold duty cracking.

chapters.title: The Second Flight
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. A contact in aviation records confirms a pattern: the erased flight was a rehearsal. A second aircraft is scheduled to fail during the delegation's departure in four days, blamed on mechanical error. Gideon realizes the peace deal itself is the target's cover story. Emotional beat: the horror of a countdown beginning.

chapters.title: Chemistry of Forgetting
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Following the burnt-wiring smell to a maintenance hangar, Gideon finds aerosol canisters and dosing logs — the passengers were sedated and re-briefed mid-flight. They confront Renner, who admits she signed off on the 'memory hygiene protocol' believing it prevented panic. Emotional beat: betrayal by the person they'd started to trust.

chapters.title: Two Truths
chapters.summary: POV Renner. Renner weighs her orders against the evidence that the protocol's architect, Deputy Director Halvorsen, intends the second flight to actually crash. She passes Gideon a key and a warning: 'They'll erase you the way they erased the plane.' Emotional beat: loyalty choosing truth at personal ruin.

chapters.title: Erasure Pending
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Gideon is detained for 'psychological review' — a euphemism for a second dosing. In a holding room they memorize the manifest, the timeline, the hangar codes, burning facts into rhythm and rhyme the way they once memorized speeches. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into discipline.

chapters.title: Departure Board, Burning
chapters.summary: POV Gideon and alternating Renner. On departure day, Gideon escapes review, reaches the terminal PA and the press riser, and reads the true manifest and flight logs aloud as the sabotaged aircraft rolls for takeoff. Halvorsen orders it grounded rather than let the record match the crash. Climax: truth as a weapon fired in public.

chapters.title: The Only Copy
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Halvorsen is arrested; the peace deal collapses anyway, but no one dies. Gideon, professionally finished and quietly dosed once more — though they faked swallowing the tablets — keeps the handwritten notes in a shoebox. Final beat: identity reduced to memory, and memory chosen freely.
